mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen for three consecutive weeks (-24.6 to -21.6), indicating a steady return to in-person work routines. This commuting recovery mechanically raises adjacent retail and recreation footfall over the following month.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose monotonically each of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is not higher than the prior 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to rise, falsifying the commuting-driven footfall link.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT usage has improved by more than 3 points over the last three weeks, crossing a threshold that signals renewed willingness to travel beyond the home. This behavioral normalization feeds into higher retail and recreation visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 points cumulative over 3 weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -37.0 to -33.4 over three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of TRANSIT crossing the 3-point cumulative improvement threshold in two or more replications.

mechanism_narrative: When both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise together, the combined effect of more commuting trips and more transit-enabled travel compounds to produce a larger lift in RETAIL_REC than either series would alone, because commute trips are frequently chained with retail stops.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:both series improved concurrently over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward change is no larger when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise jointly than when only one rises, indicating no compounding interaction.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility declined in the most recent week (13.4 to 12.1) after three weeks of increase, suggesting households are spending relatively less time at home. In a reopening regime this reduction in home-centric behavior translates into increased retail and recreation activity within one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines week-on-week after a prior rising streak
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 13.4 to 12.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following a RESIDENTIAL decline, or RESIDENTIAL resumes its upward trend instead.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS rebound in the latest week (-34.9 to -23.1) reflects a late-summer seasonal window of favorable weather. As autumn progresses and this seasonal window closes, outdoor-linked recreation activity that spills into retail-adjacent visits will recede, pulling RETAIL_REC down over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls back below -30 after the current rebound
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped 11.8 points in the latest week after three weeks of decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 28 days even as PARKS mobility declines seasonally, indicating no seasonal spillover from parks to retail.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stayed within a narrow band (-0.3 to 3.3) with no sign of panic-buying spikes, indicating the absence of new restriction announcements. In a steady policy regime this stability supports a continued gradual recovery in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains within a +/-5 point band for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged only between -0.3 and 3.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable, or GROCERY_PHARM itself spikes sharply signaling a policy shock not captured by this hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous pattern of rising WORKPLACES and falling RESIDENTIAL indicates a genuine behavioral pivot away from home-bound routines toward out-of-home activity, which jointly predicts a stronger increase in RETAIL_REC than either series moving alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose while RESIDENTIAL fell in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week change is not larger during weeks when WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls simultaneously compared to weeks when only one condition holds.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself jumped by 2.9 points in the latest week, the largest single-week gain in the snapshot. A weekly gain exceeding 2 points signals building momentum that tends to persist into the following week due to habit formation around reopened venues.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -31.0 to -28.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stays flat in the week immediately following a greater-than-2-point weekly gain, breaking the momentum persistence assumption.
